turns.assessment: The rising bias current suggests the transmitter control loop may be compensating for laser ageing or temperature, but laser-bias drift is not a documented fault mode for this line interface. A documented TX_LASER_FAIL would cause loss of the channel at the far-end receiver; unchanged receiver, optical-quality, and line-monitoring metrics strongly contradict that condition. No repair should be committed from the current evidence; continue lifecycle/trend monitoring under normal maintenance policy.

proposals.rationale: This is the only documented transmitter-laser fault on the indicated interface, but it is a hard failure expected to remove the transmitted signal. The absence of alarms, service impact, or changes at the far end makes an actual TX_LASER_FAIL very unlikely.

score.why: cause flagged as unconsidered and absent
